At the zoo gate

Every animal today is an idea of Jesus, because "all things were made by him" (John 1:3). Start with this 5-minute devotional before you go in.

Read together "But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee; and the fowls of the air, and they shall tell thee" (Job 12:7).

Think about it Jesus loved to teach with animals. He talked about sheep, sparrows, fish, foxes, a hen and her chicks, and even a camel squeezing through a needle. Ellen White explains: "The parables by which, during His ministry, He loved to teach His lessons of truth show how open His spirit was to the influences of nature" (The Desire of Ages, p. 70).

Ellen White "Nature and revelation alike testify of God's love" (Steps to Christ, p. 9). "Upon all created things is seen the impress of the Deity. Nature testifies of God" (Education, p. 99).

Pray "Dear Jesus, thank You for making every animal. Open our eyes today to see what You want to teach us about You. Amen."

Gate questions

  1. Who made all the animals?

    God. The Bible says Jesus was there making them (John 1:3, Colossians 1:16).

  2. On which days of Creation were the animals made?

    Fish and birds on day 5. Land animals on day 6, the same day as people (Genesis 1:20-25).

  3. Who gave the animals their names?

    Adam (Genesis 2:19-20). Bonus: what name would you give a brand-new animal?

  4. In Eden, did lions eat other animals?

    No. God gave every animal plants to eat (Genesis 1:30). Fear and hunting came after sin. In God's new earth "the wolf also shall dwell with the lamb" again (Isaiah 11:6).

How to use the lessons

  1. Pick 8 to 12 animals the kids love. Each lesson takes about 3 minutes at the enclosure.
  2. One child reads "Did you know?" out loud while everyone watches the animal.
  3. A parent reads the Bible part and asks: "What does this teach us about Jesus?"
  4. Ask the questions. Give a point per right answer, or let the kids quiz you.
  5. Tick the animal off in the checklist at the end.

Dutch names are in the headings so the kids can match them to the zoo signs. Bible quotes are from the King James Version.

African savanna

The savanna animals show God's power and His care: the strongest lion and the smallest hyrax both point to Jesus.

LionLeeuw

Did you know? A lion's roar can be heard about 8 km away. Lions rest up to 20 hours a day. They are the only cats that live in family groups, called prides.

Bible Jesus is called "the Lion of the tribe of Juda" (Revelation 5:5): a strong, brave King who wins against evil. One verse later He is a Lamb that was slain (Revelation 5:6). Our mighty King gave His life for us. When Daniel was thrown to the lions, "God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths" (Daniel 6:22).

Ellen White "God did not prevent Daniel's enemies from casting him into the lions' den; ... but it was that He might make the deliverance of His servant more marked." And: "Heaven is very near those who suffer for righteousness' sake" (Prophets and Kings, pp. 543, 545).
  1. Why is Jesus called both a Lion and a Lamb?

    He is a strong King (Lion) who gave Himself for our sins (Lamb). Both are in Revelation 5:5-6.

  2. Who shut the lions' mouths for Daniel?

    An angel God sent (Daniel 6:22).

  3. Proverbs 28:1 says "the righteous are bold as a..."?

    Lion. With Jesus we don't have to be afraid.

Try this Roar together as loud as you can. Then whisper: "Jesus is stronger."

GiraffeGiraf

Did you know? The giraffe is the tallest animal, up to about 5.5 m. Its neck has 7 bones, the same number as yours. Its heart weighs about 11 kg. Its tongue is about 45 cm long and dark blue-black, which protects it from sunburn.

Bible A giraffe spends its day looking up. "I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help. My help cometh from the LORD" (Psalm 121:1-2). And its giant heart reminds us of God's promise: "A new heart also will I give you" (Ezekiel 36:26). Jesus gives us a big heart full of His love.

  1. How many neck bones does a giraffe have?

    Seven, just like you. God used one plan for very different sizes.

  2. Why does a giraffe need such a big heart?

    To pump blood all the way up its long neck to its brain.

  3. Where does our help come from?

    From the LORD, who made heaven and earth (Psalm 121:2).

Try this Stretch up on tiptoe like a giraffe and say: "My help comes from the Lord!"

ZebraZebra

Did you know? No two zebras have the same stripes, just like your fingerprints. A foal learns its mother's stripes, voice and smell in its first days so it can find her in the herd. When a lion comes, the herd bunches together and all the stripes make it hard to pick one out.

Bible God knows you personally: "I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine" (Isaiah 43:1). You are "fearfully and wonderfully made" (Psalm 139:14). Zebras are safer together, and so are Christians: "not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together" (Hebrews 10:25).

  1. Do two zebras ever have the same stripes?

    No. Every zebra is one of a kind, and so are you.

  2. How does a baby zebra find its mother?

    It knows her stripes, voice and smell. Jesus says: "My sheep hear my voice" (John 10:27).

  3. Is a zebra white with black stripes or black with white stripes?

    Its skin underneath is dark, so many scientists say black with white stripes.

ElephantOlifant

Did you know? The elephant is the biggest land animal. Its trunk has no bones but tens of thousands of tiny muscle bundles, strong enough to lift a log and gentle enough to pick up a peanut. It eats up to about 150 kg of food a day. A baby grows inside its mother for about 22 months, almost two years. The oldest female, the matriarch, leads the herd and remembers where the water is.

Bible God describes a giant animal, behemoth: "He is the chief of the ways of God" (Job 40:19). Some think of an elephant or a hippo. Nothing is too big for the God who made it. The grandmother elephant leads her family to water; Jesus leads us to the water of life: "whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst" (John 4:14).

  1. How long is a baby elephant inside its mother?

    About 22 months, longer than any other land animal.

  2. Who leads the elephant herd to water?

    The oldest grandmother. Who leads us to living water? Jesus (John 4:14).

  3. Elephants never forget. What does Ecclesiastes 12:1 ask young people to remember?

    "Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth."

RhinocerosNeushoorn

Did you know? A rhino's horn is made of keratin, the same stuff as your fingernails. Rhinos see poorly but smell and hear very well. They love mud baths, which work as sunscreen and bug spray.

Bible A rhino can't see far, so it trusts its nose and ears. We can't see Jesus yet, but we hear Him in His Word: "For we walk by faith, not by sight" (2 Corinthians 5:7), and "faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God" (Romans 10:17).

  1. What is a rhino horn made of?

    Keratin, like your nails. Bite your nails and you're nibbling rhino horn material!

  2. How do we follow Jesus when we can't see Him?

    By faith, by listening to His Word and praying.

  3. The King James Bible mentions a "unicorn" (Numbers 23:22). Was it a horse with a horn?

    No. The Hebrew word means a strong wild animal, probably a wild ox.

HippopotamusNijlpaard

Did you know? Hippos can't really swim. They walk or bounce along the river bottom and can hold their breath for about 5 minutes. Their skin makes a red-orange liquid, sometimes called "blood sweat", that works as sunscreen. Hippopotamus means "river horse" in Greek; nijlpaard means "Nile horse".

Bible The hippo doesn't swim over deep water; it walks through it. God promises: "When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee" (Isaiah 43:2). And just as God gave the hippo its own sunscreen, He covers us: "He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust" (Psalm 91:4).

  1. Can hippos swim?

    Not really. They walk or bounce along the bottom.

  2. What does God promise when life feels like deep water?

    "I will be with thee" (Isaiah 43:2).

  3. What does nijlpaard mean?

    Nile horse.

MeerkatStokstaartje

Did you know? Meerkats live in groups in underground burrows. While the others dig for food, one meerkat stands guard as the sentinel, and they take turns. They have one alarm call for eagles in the sky and another for danger on the ground.

Bible Jesus told His friends: "Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation" (Matthew 26:41). He also told us to watch and be ready for His coming (Mark 13:37). Meerkats look out for each other: "Bear ye one another's burdens" (Galatians 6:2).

  1. What does the guard meerkat do?

    Watches for danger and calls a warning so the others can hide.

  2. What did Jesus say to do so we won't fall into temptation?

    "Watch and pray" (Matthew 26:41).

  3. How can you be a guard meerkat for your brother or sister?

    Look out for them, warn them kindly, and pray for them.

Try this Stand tall like a sentinel and name one person you will pray for today.

Rock hyraxKlipdas

Did you know? The rock hyrax looks like a big guinea pig, but its closest living relatives are elephants and sea cows. Its rubbery, sweaty foot pads grip rocks like suction cups. A colony suns itself on the rocks while one keeps lookout. Few Dutch zoos keep them; Diergaarde Blijdorp is one.

Bible "The conies are but a feeble folk, yet make they their houses in the rocks" (Proverbs 30:26). The coney is this rock hyrax! It is small and weak, but safe because it hides in the rock. Jesus is our Rock: "The LORD is my rock, and my fortress" (Psalm 18:2), and "that Rock was Christ" (1 Corinthians 10:4).

  1. Which animal in the Bible makes its house in the rocks?

    The coney, which is the rock hyrax (Proverbs 30:26).

  2. Who is our Rock?

    Jesus (1 Corinthians 10:4).

  3. Which giant animal is the hyrax related to?

    The elephant!

Try this Sing "The wise man built his house upon the rock" (Matthew 7:24).

Apes and monkeys

Apes are clever and caring, but only people are made in God's image, and Jesus became a human to save us.

Ellen White "Man was to bear God's image, both in outward resemblance and in character" (Patriarchs and Prophets, p. 45).

GorillaGorilla

Did you know? The gorilla is the biggest ape. A grown male, the silverback, can weigh about 180 kg. Gorillas eat mostly leaves, stems and fruit. Every evening they build a fresh nest of leaves to sleep in. A silverback beats his chest to warn, not to start a fight, and is gentle with the little ones.

Bible A brand-new nest every night reminds us that God's love is fresh every day: "his compassions fail not. They are new every morning" (Lamentations 3:22-23). The strong silverback is gentle with babies, just like Jesus: "He shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom" (Isaiah 40:11).

  1. How often does a gorilla make a new bed?

    Every night.

  2. What is new every morning, according to Lamentations 3:23?

    God's mercies.

  3. Jesus is strong. How was He with children?

    Gentle and kind. He said "Suffer little children to come unto me" (Mark 10:14).

ChimpanzeeChimpansee

Did you know? Chimps use tools. They poke sticks into termite mounds to "fish" for termites and crack nuts with stones. They laugh when they are tickled. After a quarrel they make up with hugs, kisses and grooming.

Bible Chimps are smart, but only people are made "in the image of God" (Genesis 1:27). Only we can pray, read God's Word and choose to love Him. Chimps make up after a fight; God asks us to do the same: "be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you" (Ephesians 4:32).

  1. What tool does a chimp use to catch termites?

    A stick or a grass stem.

  2. What makes people different from every animal?

    We are made in God's image (Genesis 1:27). We can know God, pray and worship Him.

  3. How do chimps make up after a fight? How do we?

    Chimps hug and groom. We say sorry and forgive, because Jesus forgave us (Ephesians 4:32).

OrangutanOrang-oetan

Did you know? Orangutan comes from the Malay words for "person of the forest". It is the biggest animal that lives in trees. A baby stays with its mother for about 7 or 8 years, the longest childhood of any animal except humans. In the rain an orangutan holds a big leaf over its head as an umbrella.

Bible An orangutan mother never leaves her baby. God loves you even more: "Can a woman forget her sucking child...? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee" (Isaiah 49:15). "As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you" (Isaiah 66:13).

  1. How long does a baby orangutan stay with its mother?

    About 7 or 8 years.

  2. What does God promise in Isaiah 49:15?

    He will never forget you.

  3. What does orangutan mean?

    Person of the forest.

Try this Give your mum or dad a baby-orangutan hug.

Ring-tailed lemurRingstaartmaki

Did you know? Ring-tailed lemurs live in the wild only on Madagascar. Every morning they sit with their arms open and belly toward the sun to warm up. Males have "stink fights": they rub smelly scent on their tails and wave them at each other.

Bible The lemur starts its day in the sun. We start ours with the Son! Jesus said "I am the light of the world" (John 8:12). He Himself rose "a great while before day" to pray (Mark 1:35). And for stink fights the Bible has a better idea: "A soft answer turneth away wrath" (Proverbs 15:1).

  1. Why do lemurs sit in the sun in the morning?

    To warm up after the cool night.

  2. When did Jesus pray?

    Early in the morning, before sunrise (Mark 1:35).

  3. What turns away anger better than a stink fight?

    A soft, kind answer (Proverbs 15:1).

Try this Do the lemur sun pose together and say a one-sentence morning prayer.

BaboonBaviaan

Did you know? Baboons live in big troops and groom each other to stay clean and show friendship. In ancient Egypt the hamadryas baboon was a holy animal, linked to one of their gods.

Bible King Solomon's ships brought "gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks" (1 Kings 10:22). Egypt worshipped animals, but God calls us to "worship him that made heaven, and earth, and the sea" (Revelation 14:7). We admire the baboon and worship its Maker.

  1. Which king had apes and peacocks brought by ship?

    King Solomon (1 Kings 10:22).

  2. People in Egypt worshipped baboons. Whom do we worship?

    The Creator, not the creature (Revelation 14:7, Romans 1:25).

  3. Baboons show friendship by grooming. How can you show friendship today?

    Let the kids answer: share, help, say something kind.

Desert, Asia and the far north

From the hot desert to the Arctic ice, these animals teach kindness, rest, courage and how Jesus makes us new.

CamelKameel en dromedaris

Did you know? A camel's hump stores fat, not water. A very thirsty camel can drink about 135 litres in 13 minutes. It has two rows of long eyelashes and can close its nostrils against blowing sand. Easy trick: a dromedary has one hump (lay a D on its side), a Bactrian camel has two (lay a B on its side).

Bible When Abraham's servant asked Rebekah for a drink, she said: "I will draw water for thy camels also, until they have done drinking" (Genesis 24:19). He had ten camels! She went the extra mile, just as Jesus taught: "whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain" (Matthew 5:41). Jesus also said it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter God's kingdom, but "with God all things are possible" (Matthew 19:24-26).

Ellen White Abraham's servant noticed Rebekah because "her ready courtesy gave evidence of a kind heart and an active, energetic nature" (Patriarchs and Prophets, pp. 172-173).
  1. What is inside a camel's hump?

    Fat, which gives energy on long trips.

  2. How many camels did Rebekah give water to?

    Ten (Genesis 24:10). If they were very thirsty, that could be more than 1,000 litres!

  3. What is impossible for people but possible for God?

    Saving us (Matthew 19:26).

TigerTijger

Did you know? The tiger is the biggest cat in the world. Its skin is striped too, not just its fur, and no two tigers have the same stripes. Unlike most cats, tigers love water and swim well.

Bible "Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots?" (Jeremiah 13:23). A tiger can't wash off its stripes, and we can't wash away our sin by ourselves. But Jesus can make us new: "if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature" (2 Corinthians 5:17).

  1. If a tiger had no fur, would you still see stripes?

    Yes, its skin is striped too.

  2. Can a leopard change its spots?

    No (Jeremiah 13:23). But Jesus can change our hearts (2 Corinthians 5:17).

  3. What did David pray in Psalm 51:10?

    "Create in me a clean heart, O God."

Red pandaRode panda

Did you know? The red panda is about the size of a cat and eats mostly bamboo leaves. A long wrist bone works as an extra "thumb" to hold bamboo. It sleeps a lot high in the trees, with its bushy tail wrapped around it like a blanket. It was called a panda before the giant panda was.

Bible The red panda knows how to rest. Jesus says: "Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest" (Matthew 11:28). God even gave us a weekly day of rest, the Sabbath: "The sabbath was made for man" (Mark 2:27).

  1. What does a red panda use as a blanket?

    Its tail.

  2. What does Jesus give tired people?

    Rest (Matthew 11:28).

  3. Which day did God bless as a day of rest?

    The seventh day, the Sabbath (Exodus 20:8-11).

Brown bearBruine beer

Did you know? Brown bears sleep through much of the winter in a den, living off their fat. They have a super sense of smell and can run about 50 km/h. Mother bears fiercely protect their cubs.

Bible Young David protected his father's sheep from a lion and a bear. Later he said: "The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine" (1 Samuel 17:37). Remembering how God helped him gave David courage to face Goliath. Jesus is the Good Shepherd who protects us (John 10:11).

Ellen White Out in the fields with the sheep, "God was teaching David lessons of trust." Caring for his flock, David was learning how much "the Great Shepherd" cares for His sheep (Patriarchs and Prophets, p. 644).
  1. Which two wild animals did David fight to save his sheep?

    A lion and a bear (1 Samuel 17:34-36).

  2. What gave David courage to face Goliath?

    Remembering how God had helped him before.

  3. Why do bears sleep through winter?

    There is little food, so they rest and live off their fat.

Polar bearIJsbeer

Did you know? A polar bear's skin is black. Its hairs are see-through and only look white in the light. It can smell a seal more than 1 km away, even under about 1 m of snow. Its huge paws spread its weight on thin ice like snowshoes.

Bible "Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow" (Isaiah 1:18). The polar bear isn't really white underneath, and we aren't good on our own. But Jesus covers us with His goodness, "the robe of righteousness" (Isaiah 61:10).

  1. What colour is a polar bear's skin?

    Black.

  2. What does God promise to do with our sins?

    Make them white as snow (Isaiah 1:18).

  3. God asked Job: "Hast thou entered into the treasures of the..."?

    Snow (Job 38:22).

WolfWolf

Did you know? Wolves live in families called packs, led by the mother and father. They howl to talk to the pack across long distances. Wild wolves have come back to the Netherlands; the first ones settled on the Veluwe in 2018, and in 2019 the first wild pups in about 200 years were born.

Bible Jesus said: "The good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep." A hired man "seeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and fleeth" (John 10:11-12). Jesus never runs away from us; He gave His life for us. And one day "the wolf also shall dwell with the lamb" (Isaiah 11:6).

  1. What does the Good Shepherd do when the wolf comes?

    He stays and protects the sheep, even giving His life (John 10:11).

  2. Where will the wolf and the lamb live together in peace?

    In God's new earth (Isaiah 11:6, 65:25).

  3. What did Jesus mean by wolves "in sheep's clothing" (Matthew 7:15)?

    People who look good but teach wrong things. We check everything with the Bible.

Birds

Jesus said God feeds the birds and knows when a sparrow falls (Matthew 6:26, 10:29), so every bird here is a reminder that He cares for you.

Ellen White "He who upholds the unnumbered worlds throughout immensity, at the same time cares for the wants of the little brown sparrow that sings its humble song without fear" (Steps to Christ, p. 86).

PenguinPinguïn

Did you know? Penguins can't fly in the air, but they "fly" underwater with their flipper-wings. Dutch zoos keep Humboldt penguins from South America (Wildlands) and African penguins (ARTIS, Burgers' Zoo). Emperor penguin dads hold the egg on their feet for about two months in the freezing Antarctic winter, eating almost nothing. In the cold, penguins huddle together to share warmth.

Bible "If two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone?" (Ecclesiastes 4:11). Penguins can't fly like eagles, but God made them champion swimmers. God gives each of us different gifts to use for others (1 Peter 4:10).

  1. Can penguins fly?

    Not in the air, but they fly underwater.

  2. How do penguins stay warm?

    They huddle together, just like Ecclesiastes 4:11 says.

  3. What gift has God given you?

    Let each child name one, then name one for a brother or sister.

FlamingoFlamingo

Did you know? Flamingos are pink because of their food: tiny shrimp and algae full of pink-orange colour. Chicks hatch grey-white. Flamingos often stand and even sleep on one leg, and they eat with their heads upside down in the water.

Bible A flamingo becomes the colour of what it eats. We become like what we look at and listen to: "beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image" (2 Corinthians 3:18). So "whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely... think on these things" (Philippians 4:8).

Ellen White "It is a law both of the intellectual and the spiritual nature that by beholding we become changed" (The Great Controversy, p. 555).
  1. Why is a flamingo pink?

    Because of the colour in its food.

  2. How do we become more like Jesus?

    By looking at Him: reading about Him, singing to Him and talking with Him (2 Corinthians 3:18).

Try this Stand on one leg like a flamingo. Who can say Philippians 4:8 (or part of it) before wobbling?

EagleArend

Did you know? Eagles see 4 to 8 times sharper than people and can spot a rabbit from far away. They soar for hours on rising warm air, hardly flapping their wings.

Bible "They that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary" (Isaiah 40:31). The eagle doesn't fly by its own strength alone; it rests on the rising air. We rest on God's strength. A mother eagle stirs up the nest to teach her young to fly, then catches them on her wings, and God teaches us the same way (Deuteronomy 32:11).

Ellen White She tells of an eagle in the Alps that a storm beat down into a narrow mountain valley. At last "she darts upward, and, piercing the clouds, is once more in the clear sunlight." Then she gives the lesson: "Into the sunlight of His presence we may rise on the wings of faith" (Education, pp. 118-119).
  1. How does an eagle fly for hours without flapping?

    It rides on rising warm air.

  2. Who "shall mount up with wings as eagles"?

    "They that wait upon the LORD" (Isaiah 40:31).

  3. What did the eagle in the storm do?

    It flew up through the clouds to the sunshine. When life is stormy, we look up to Jesus.

OstrichStruisvogel

Did you know? The ostrich is the biggest bird in the world. It can't fly but can run about 70 km/h. Its egg weighs about 1.4 kg, as much as about 24 chicken eggs. Its eye is bigger than its brain! And no, ostriches don't bury their heads in the sand.

Bible God Himself describes the ostrich in Job 39:13-18. He says it isn't very wise, yet "she scorneth the horse and his rider" because she runs so fast. God made every creature with its own gift, even a funny one. And instead of hiding our heads from problems, we can bring them to Jesus: "Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you" (1 Peter 5:7).

  1. Does an ostrich bury its head in the sand?

    No, that is a myth.

  2. How many chicken eggs fit in one ostrich egg?

    About 24.

  3. What can we do with our worries instead of hiding from them?

    Give them to Jesus, because He cares for us (1 Peter 5:7).

OwlUil

Did you know? Owls can turn their heads about 270 degrees, three-quarters of the way round, because their eyes can't move in their sockets. Soft-edged feathers let them fly almost silently. Some owls can hear a mouse moving under the snow.

Bible The owl is awake at night, but God is always awake: "he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep" (Psalm 121:4). Even at night He sees perfectly: "the darkness and the light are both alike to thee" (Psalm 139:12).

  1. How far can an owl turn its head?

    About three-quarters of the way round.

  2. Who watches over you all night long?

    God, who never sleeps (Psalm 121:4).

  3. Is the dark dark to God?

    No. Darkness and light are the same to Him (Psalm 139:12).

ParrotPapegaai

Did you know? Parrots learn to talk by copying what they hear. A famous African grey parrot called Alex learned more than 100 words. Large macaws can live 50 years or more. Parrots have two toes in front and two behind, so they can hold food like a hand.

Bible A parrot becomes like the voices around it. Whom do we copy? "Be ye therefore followers of God, as dear children" (Ephesians 5:1). And our words matter: "Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O LORD" (Psalm 19:14).

  1. How does a parrot learn to talk?

    By hearing the same words again and again and copying them.

  2. Whom should we copy?

    Jesus (Ephesians 5:1, 1 Peter 2:21).

Try this Play parrot. One person says a short Bible verse, everyone repeats it in a parrot voice.

PeacockPauw

Did you know? The male is the peacock and the female the peahen. His train has about 200 feathers with "eyes". The colours are not paint: tiny structures in the feathers bend the light, so they shine only when light hits them. Many Dutch zoos let peacocks walk around freely, so listen for their loud call.

Bible King Solomon's ships brought peacocks (1 Kings 10:22). A peacock shines only in the light; we shine when we reflect Jesus: "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father" (Matthew 5:16). And God cares more about the heart than about fancy feathers: "the LORD looketh on the heart" (1 Samuel 16:7).

  1. What is a female peacock called?

    A peahen.

  2. Why do the feathers sparkle?

    They reflect light. We sparkle when we reflect Jesus (Matthew 5:16).

  3. What does God look at most?

    The heart (1 Samuel 16:7).

StorkOoievaar

Did you know? White storks fly thousands of kilometres to Africa or Spain for the winter and come back in spring. Around 1970 fewer than 10 pairs were left in the Netherlands. Thanks to protection, about 2,000 pairs nested here in 2025. Storks don't sing; they clatter their beaks.

Bible "Yea, the stork in the heaven knoweth her appointed times... but my people know not the judgment of the LORD" (Jeremiah 8:7). The stork knows when it is time to travel. Jesus asks us to know the signs of His coming and be ready: "be ye also ready" (Matthew 24:44).

  1. Where do many Dutch storks go in winter?

    To Africa or Spain.

  2. What does the stork know, according to Jeremiah 8:7?

    Her appointed times.

  3. What big event should we be ready for?

    Jesus coming again (Matthew 24:44).

Dove and pigeonDuif

Did you know? You will see wild pigeons all over the zoo! Homing pigeons can find their way home from hundreds of kilometres away, using the sun and the earth's magnetism. Pigeon racing is a famous Dutch hobby.

Bible Noah's dove brought back an olive leaf (Genesis 8:11). At Jesus' baptism the Spirit came down "like a dove" and the Father said: "This is my beloved Son" (Matthew 3:16-17). When baby Jesus was brought to the temple, Mary and Joseph gave "a pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons" (Luke 2:24), the gift of a poor family. Jesus became poor so we could become rich (2 Corinthians 8:9).

Ellen White At Jesus' baptism she describes "a dovelike form of purest light,—fit emblem of Him, the meek and lowly One" (The Desire of Ages, p. 112).
  1. What did Noah's dove bring back?

    An olive leaf (Genesis 8:11).

  2. When did the Holy Spirit come down like a dove?

    At Jesus' baptism (Matthew 3:16).

  3. What did Mary and Joseph give at the temple?

    Two turtledoves or two young pigeons (Luke 2:24).

Reptiles and amphibians

In the reptile house the Bible stories get exciting: the serpent in Eden, the bronze snake, leviathan and the frogs of Egypt all point to Jesus.

SnakeSlang

Did you know? Snakes smell with their tongues: each flick picks up smells for a special organ in the roof of the mouth. They have no eyelids; a clear scale covers each eye. They have no outer ears but feel vibrations through the ground. They shed their skin in one piece.

Bible Satan used a serpent to tempt Eve (Genesis 3). Right away God gave the first promise of Jesus: the woman's descendant would crush the serpent's head (Genesis 3:15). Later, Israelites bitten by snakes were healed when they looked at a bronze snake on a pole (Numbers 21:8-9). Jesus said: "as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up" (John 3:14). We look to Jesus on the cross and live.

Ellen White Before sin, "the serpent was then one of the wisest and most beautiful creatures on the earth. It had wings," and it shone with "the color and brilliancy of burnished gold" (Patriarchs and Prophets, p. 53). About the bronze snake she writes: "So the sinner may look to Christ, and live" (p. 431).
  1. How does a snake smell?

    With its tongue.

  2. What is the very first promise of Jesus in the Bible?

    That the woman's seed would crush the serpent's head (Genesis 3:15).

  3. What did bitten Israelites have to do to live?

    Look at the bronze snake (Numbers 21:8-9). We look to Jesus (John 3:14-15).

CrocodileKrokodil

Did you know? A crocodile can replace each tooth up to about 50 times. It can go months without eating. Crocodiles have one of the strongest bites ever measured, yet a mother carries her newly hatched babies gently in her mouth.

Bible God describes leviathan, an armoured creature many think was like a crocodile: "Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook?" (Job 41:1). No person can tame it, but God made it and is far stronger: "who then is able to stand before me?" (Job 41:10). Psalm 104:26 even says God made leviathan "to play" in the sea. Nothing scary is stronger than our God.

  1. How many times can a crocodile replace a tooth?

    Up to about 50 times.

  2. How does a mother crocodile carry her babies?

    Gently, in her mouth.

  3. Who is stronger than leviathan?

    God, who made it (Job 41:10).

Giant tortoiseReuzenschildpad

Did you know? Giant tortoises can live more than 150 years. Jonathan, a tortoise on the island of St Helena, hatched around 1832, which makes him about 194 years old. A tortoise's shell is part of its skeleton, so it can never crawl out of it.

Bible God is older than the oldest tortoise: "from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God" (Psalm 90:2). A tortoise always has its home with it. Jesus asks us to stay close to Him always: "Abide in me, and I in you" (John 15:4).

  1. Can a tortoise crawl out of its shell?

    No, the shell is part of its body.

  2. Who is older than the oldest tortoise?

    God, who is "from everlasting to everlasting" (Psalm 90:2).

  3. Which fruit of the Spirit is the tortoise good at?

    Patience, called longsuffering in Galatians 5:22.

FrogKikker

Did you know? Poison dart frogs have bright colours that say "don't eat me!" Their poison comes from the insects they eat in the wild, so frogs raised in a zoo are not poisonous. Frogs drink through their skin, and they start life as tadpoles.

Bible In the second plague, frogs filled Egypt, even beds and ovens (Exodus 8:3). Moses asked Pharaoh when he wanted the frogs gone. Pharaoh answered: "To morrow" (Exodus 8:10). One more night with the frogs! God says the best time to follow Him is right now: "behold, now is the day of salvation" (2 Corinthians 6:2).

  1. Moses asked when the frogs should go. What did Pharaoh say?

    "Tomorrow!" (Exodus 8:10).

  2. When is the best time to follow Jesus?

    Today (2 Corinthians 6:2, Hebrews 3:15).

  3. Why aren't zoo poison frogs dangerous?

    Their poison comes from their wild food.

Try this Everyone croaks together: "Not tomorrow, today!"

ChameleonKameleon

Did you know? Chameleons change colour mostly to show their mood and control their temperature, not just to hide. Each eye moves on its own, so a chameleon can look forward and backward at the same time. Its tongue can shoot out up to about twice its body length, faster than you can blink.

Bible "Be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind" (Romans 12:2). Daniel didn't just blend in in Babylon; he stayed true to God (Daniel 1:8). A chameleon can look two ways at once, but Jesus said: "No man can serve two masters" (Matthew 6:24).

  1. Why does a chameleon change colour?

    Mostly to show its mood and to warm up or cool down.

  2. A chameleon can look two ways at once. Can we follow two masters?

    No (Matthew 6:24).

  3. Who stayed true to God in a foreign land instead of blending in?

    Daniel (Daniel 1:8).

Ocean and aquarium

Jesus spent much of His life by the sea and chose fishermen as His first disciples, so the aquarium is full of His stories.

Sea lion and sealZeeleeuw en zeehond

Did you know? Sea lions have small ear flaps and can "walk" on all four flippers. Seals have only ear holes and wiggle along on their bellies. Wild Dutch seals live in the Wadden Sea, and seal centres like the one in Pieterburen rescue sick or lost pups and return them to the sea. A seal's whiskers can feel the tiny water ripples of a swimming fish.

Bible "God created great whales, and every living creature that moveth, which the waters brought forth abundantly" (Genesis 1:21). Like the seal rescuers, Jesus came to find those who are lost: "the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost" (Luke 19:10).

  1. How can you tell a sea lion from a seal?

    Sea lions have ear flaps and walk on their flippers. Seals have no flaps and wiggle.

  2. Where do wild seals live in the Netherlands?

    In the Wadden Sea and the North Sea.

  3. Who came to rescue the lost?

    Jesus (Luke 19:10).

SharkHaai

Did you know? Some sharks lose and regrow thousands of teeth in their lifetime. Sharks can sense the tiny electric signals made by other animals' muscles, even a fish hiding in the sand. Their skin feels like sandpaper. Most kinds of sharks are not dangerous to people.

Bible A shark can find a fish hidden in the sand. Nothing at all is hidden from God: "Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight" (Hebrews 4:13). But God doesn't search for us to catch us; He knows us and loves us: "O LORD, thou hast searched me, and known me" (Psalm 139:1).

  1. About how many teeth can a shark use up in its life?

    Thousands.

  2. Can anything hide from God?

    No (Hebrews 4:13). And He loves us completely.

  3. What does shark skin feel like?

    Sandpaper.

JellyfishKwal

Did you know? A jellyfish is about 95% water. It has no brain, heart, bones or blood. Most jellyfish drift wherever the current takes them, and some even glow in the dark.

Bible God doesn't want us to be like jellyfish, "tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine" (Ephesians 4:14). He wants us "rooted and built up in him" (Colossians 2:7). A jellyfish has no backbone, but God says: "Be strong and of a good courage... for the LORD thy God is with thee" (Joshua 1:9).

  1. What is a jellyfish mostly made of?

    Water.

  2. Does a jellyfish have a brain?

    No!

  3. How do we keep from drifting like a jellyfish?

    By staying rooted in Jesus: reading His Word and praying every day (Colossians 2:7).

ClownfishClownvis

Did you know? The clownfish lives among the stinging tentacles of a sea anemone. A slimy coat keeps it from being stung. The clownfish cleans the anemone and chases away fish that want to eat it, and the anemone protects the clownfish.

Bible The clownfish is safe in a place where others get stung. We are safe in Jesus: "your life is hid with Christ in God" (Colossians 3:3). "He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty" (Psalm 91:1).

  1. Why doesn't the anemone sting the clownfish?

    Its slimy coat protects it.

  2. Where is our safe hiding place?

    In Jesus (Colossians 3:3, Psalm 91:1).

  3. What does the clownfish do for the anemone?

    Cleans it and protects it. Friends help each other.

FishVissen

Did you know? Fish breathe with gills that take oxygen out of the water. Many fish swim in schools, turning together as if they were one animal.

Bible Jesus called fishermen: "Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men" (Matthew 4:19). He fed 5,000 people with a boy's five loaves and two small fishes (John 6:9-11). After He rose, the disciples caught exactly 153 fish (John 21:11). Jesus also said that as Jonah was three days in the great fish, He would be three days in the grave (Matthew 12:40). Early Christians drew a simple fish as a secret sign: the Greek word for fish, ICHTHYS, spells the first letters of "Jesus Christ, God's Son, Saviour".

Ellen White Jesus filled Peter's empty nets to show that He "whose word could gather the fishes from the sea could also impress human hearts," so His followers could become "fishers of men" (The Desire of Ages, p. 249).
  1. How many fish did the disciples catch after Jesus rose?

    153 (John 21:11).

  2. What did a boy share so Jesus could feed 5,000 people?

    Five loaves and two fishes (John 6:9).

  3. What does "fishers of men" mean?

    Helping people come to know Jesus.

Try this Draw the fish sign with your finger on the glass (or on paper) and say what the letters mean.

Insects

The smallest animals carry some of the biggest lessons: new life, hard work and sharing good news.

ButterflyVlinder

Did you know? A butterfly's life has four stages: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis and butterfly. Inside the chrysalis the caterpillar's body mostly breaks down into a kind of soup and is rebuilt as a butterfly. Butterflies taste with their feet. Many Dutch zoos have a warm butterfly house where butterflies land on visitors.

Bible The caterpillar goes into the chrysalis and comes out completely new. Jesus was laid in a tomb, and on Sunday morning the angel said: "He is not here: for he is risen" (Matthew 28:6). Because He lives, we will be changed too when He comes: "we shall all be changed, In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump" (1 Corinthians 15:51-52).

Ellen White On the morning Jesus returns, "The living righteous are changed 'in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye.'" And a lovely detail for kids: "Little children are borne by holy angels to their mothers' arms" (The Great Controversy, p. 645).
  1. What are the four stages of a butterfly's life?

    Egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly.

  2. What does a butterfly taste with?

    Its feet!

  3. When will God's people be changed in the twinkling of an eye?

    When Jesus comes again (1 Corinthians 15:52).

Try this In the butterfly house, stand very still. If a butterfly lands on you, whisper: "Behold, I make all things new" (Revelation 21:5).

Leafcutter antBladsnijdersmier

Did you know? Leafcutter ants cut pieces of leaf and carry them home, many times heavier than themselves. They don't eat the leaves. They use them to grow a fungus garden, and they eat the fungus. They were farmers long before people! A colony can have millions of ants, and each ant has its own job.

Bible "Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise: Which having no guide, overseer, or ruler, Provideth her meat in the summer" (Proverbs 6:6-8). Every ant has a job, and so does every person in God's family: "For as the body is one, and hath many members" (1 Corinthians 12:12).

Ellen White "The ants teach lessons of patient industry, of perseverance in surmounting obstacles, of providence for the future" (Education, pp. 117-118).
  1. Do leafcutter ants eat the leaves?

    No. They grow fungus on them and eat that.

  2. What does Proverbs 6:6 tell a lazy person to do?

    "Go to the ant... and be wise."

  3. What job can you do in your family or church this week?

    Let each child pick one.

HoneybeeHoningbij

Did you know? To make about half a kilo of honey, bees visit around 2 million flowers. When a bee finds good flowers, it flies home and does a "waggle dance" that shows the others where to go. Bees carry pollen from flower to flower, which helps fruit grow.

Bible "How sweet are thy words unto my taste! yea, sweeter than honey to my mouth!" (Psalm 119:103). A bee that finds good flowers can't keep it to itself; it dances to tell the others. We share the good news about Jesus: "Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel" (Mark 16:15).

Ellen White "The industrious bee gives to men of intelligence an example that they would do well to imitate. These insects observe perfect order, and no idler is allowed in the hive" (Testimonies for the Church, vol. 4, p. 455).
  1. How does a bee tell the others where the flowers are?

    With a waggle dance.

  2. What is sweeter than honey?

    God's words (Psalm 119:103).

  3. Samson's riddle: "Out of the strong came forth sweetness." What was it?

    Honey that bees made inside a lion's skeleton (Judges 14:8-14).

  4. Who ate locusts and wild honey?

    John the Baptist (Matthew 3:4).

Try this Do a waggle dance, then tell someone one good thing about Jesus.

Children's farm · Kinderboerderij

The farm animals are the ones Jesus talked about most, and here the kids can touch them.

SheepSchaap

Did you know? Sheep can recognise about 50 other sheep faces and remember them for years. They know their shepherd's voice and follow it. A sheep with a heavy wool coat that rolls onto its back can't get up by itself; the shepherd has to come and turn it over.

Bible "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want" (Psalm 23:1). Jesus said: "My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me" (John 10:27). In His story, the shepherd leaves 99 sheep to find the one that is lost (Luke 15:4-7). And Jesus Himself is "the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world" (John 1:29).

Ellen White "Jesus knows us individually, and is touched with the feeling of our infirmities. He knows us all by name" (The Desire of Ages, p. 479).
  1. How many sheep did the shepherd leave to find the lost one?

    99 (Luke 15:4).

  2. What did John the Baptist call Jesus?

    "The Lamb of God" (John 1:29).

  3. A sheep stuck on its back needs help. What does Jesus do when we fall?

    He comes and lifts us up (Psalm 23:3, 145:14).

GoatGeit

Did you know? Goats have rectangular pupils, so they can see almost all the way around without turning their heads. They are amazing climbers, and some even climb trees. They don't really eat tin cans; they nibble everything because they are curious.

Bible "The high hills are a refuge for the wild goats" (Psalm 104:18). Jesus told a story of sheep and goats (Matthew 25:31-46). It isn't the goats' fault; He used them as a picture. The "sheep" were people who fed the hungry and visited the sick, and Jesus said: "Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me" (Matthew 25:40).

  1. Why are a goat's pupils rectangular?

    So it can see almost all around.

  2. In Jesus' story, what did the "sheep" do?

    They fed the hungry, gave drinks, welcomed strangers and visited the sick (Matthew 25:35-36).

  3. When you help someone, whom are you really helping?

    Jesus (Matthew 25:40).

DonkeyEzel

Did you know? Donkeys aren't stubborn, they are careful: when something feels unsafe they stop and think. Many donkeys have a dark stripe down the back and across the shoulders that forms a cross. An old legend says it is because a donkey carried Jesus. Donkeys remember places and friends for many years.

Bible Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a young donkey, just as Zechariah promised: "thy King cometh unto thee... lowly, and riding upon an ass" (Zechariah 9:9, Matthew 21:5-7). A king on a war horse comes to fight. Jesus came humble, bringing peace. Balaam's donkey saw God's angel when Balaam didn't, and God let it speak (Numbers 22:28).

Ellen White Writing about Balaam beating his donkey: "Few realize as they should the sinfulness of abusing animals or leaving them to suffer from neglect. He who created man made the lower animals also" (Patriarchs and Prophets, p. 443).
  1. Which animal did Jesus ride into Jerusalem?

    A young donkey (Matthew 21:7).

  2. Which donkey talked?

    Balaam's donkey (Numbers 22:28).

  3. What shape can you find on many donkeys' backs?

    A cross.

  4. Why are we kind to animals?

    God made them and cares for them. "A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast" (Proverbs 12:10).

ChickenKip

Did you know? A mother hen clucks to her chicks while they are still inside their eggs, and the chicks peep back. When danger comes she spreads her wings over them. Roosters have a built-in clock and often crow before sunrise.

Bible Jesus said: "how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings" (Matthew 23:37). Peter promised never to deny Jesus, but before the rooster crowed he denied Him three times (Matthew 26:34, 74-75). After Jesus rose, He forgave Peter and asked him three times: "lovest thou me?" (John 21:15-17).

Ellen White As the rooster crowed, "the Saviour turned from the frowning judges, and looked full upon His poor disciple." In Jesus' face Peter "read deep pity and sorrow, but there was no anger there" (The Desire of Ages, p. 713).
  1. What does a hen do when danger comes?

    Gathers her chicks under her wings.

  2. What happened when the rooster crowed?

    Peter remembered Jesus' words and cried (Matthew 26:75).

  3. Did Jesus forgive Peter?

    Yes. He asked three times "lovest thou me?" and gave him a job: "Feed my sheep" (John 21:17).

PigVarken

Did you know? Pigs are among the smartest animals. They can learn their names and solve puzzles. Pigs can hardly sweat, so they roll in mud to cool down and protect their skin from sunburn.

Bible In Jesus' story, a son wasted all his money and ended up feeding pigs, so hungry he wanted their food (Luke 15:15-16). He went home, and "when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him" (Luke 15:20). That is how God welcomes us back. (God also gave Israel health laws, and the pig was on the "not for eating" list, Leviticus 11:7.)

Ellen White "But while he is yet 'a great way off' the father discerns his form. Love is of quick sight" (Christ's Object Lessons, p. 203). And to us: "If you take even one step toward Him in repentance, He will hasten to enfold you in His arms of infinite love" (p. 206).
  1. What job did the lost son end up doing?

    Feeding pigs (Luke 15:15).

  2. What did the father do when he saw his son coming?

    He ran, hugged him and kissed him (Luke 15:20).

  3. Why do pigs roll in mud?

    To cool down, because they can hardly sweat.

RabbitKonijn

Did you know? A rabbit's teeth never stop growing, so it chews a lot. Rabbits eat some of their own soft droppings to digest their food a second time. A happy rabbit does a jump-and-twist in the air called a binky.

Bible Rabbits are always listening, with ears that turn toward every sound. "Let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath" (James 1:19). And a binky is a picture of joy: "This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it" (Psalm 118:24).

  1. Do a rabbit's teeth ever stop growing?

    No, never.

  2. What does James 1:19 say we should be quick to do?

    Listen.

  3. What makes you want to jump for joy like a rabbit?

    Let each child answer, then thank God for it together.

End of the day

Finish with a Bible animal hunt, a few talk questions on the way home and a thank-you prayer.

  2. Answer

Talk on the way home

  1. Which animal was your favourite today, and what did it teach you about Jesus?
  2. Which animal reminded you most of Jesus? (Lion, lamb, shepherd, mother hen... why?)
  3. Which animal showed God’s power? His care? His sense of humour?
  4. Which animal would you like to be more like this week, and how?
  5. What will animals be like when Jesus makes everything new? (Isaiah 11:6-9)

Memory verse “O LORD, how manifold are thy works! in wisdom hast thou made them all: the earth is full of thy riches” (Psalm 104:24).

Ellen White In the very last words of The Great Controversy she pictures the new earth, where everything God made, “in their unshadowed beauty and perfect joy, declare that God is love” (p. 678).

Closing prayer “Dear Jesus, thank You for every animal we saw today: the strong ones, the funny ones and the tiny ones. Thank You that You made them all and that You care for us even more. Help us to trust You like sheep trust their shepherd. We can’t wait to see the lion and the lamb together in Your new earth. Amen.”
